manna ash noun

also mountain ash, flowering ash

classical

Verg. G. 2.111 (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 3.27.58 (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 16.73 (Lewis & Short)

ornus, ornī f.

noun, second declension

a mountain ash tree

Lewis & Short calls it “the wild mountain-ash”. The identification is uncertain: botanists use the word for the manna or flowering ash (Fraxinus ornus), a small ash of southern hills; the rowan, which English also calls mountain ash, is a different tree.

Examples

  • flūminibus salicēs crassīsque palūdibus alnī nāscuntur, sterilēs saxōsīs montibus ornī

    willows grow by rivers and alders in thick marshes, barren ashes on rocky hillsVerg. G. 2.110–111

See also tree, ash, alder.

SourcesLewis & Short: ornus

Vergil, Georgica 2.110–111.
